articles.headline: Oscar winner Lupita Nyong'o invests in BAL team Nairobi City Thunder
articles.description: Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong'o announced her investment in the Nairobi City Thunder, the first Kenyan team to play at the NBA-backed Basketball Africa League (BAL), on Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: オスカー女優ルピタ・ニョンゴ、BALのナイロビ・シティ・サンダーに投資
articles.descriptionJa: アカデミー賞受賞女優のルピタ・ニョンゴは木曜日、NBAが支援するバスケットボール・アフリカ・リーグ（BAL）に出場する初のケニアチーム、ナイロビ・シティ・サンダーへの出資を発表した。
articles.body:
Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong'o announced her investment in the Nairobi City Thunder, the first Kenyan team to play at the NBA-backed Basketball Africa League (BAL), on Thursday.

Nyong'o is a citizen of Kenya, Mexico and the United States. She is the daughter of Kenyan politician and academic Peter Anyang' Nyong'o - the incumbent governor of Kisumu County - and Dorothy Nyong'o, a PR consultant who is the managing trustee of the Africa Cancer Foundation.

After her Oscar-winning breakthrough in Steve McQueen's 12 Years a Slave (2013), Mexico City-born Lupita Nyong'o shot to fame and has never looked back.

The actress, who notably starred in Black Panther (2018), Us (2019) and The Odyssey (2026), wrote on Instagram on Thursday: "Taking a tunnel walk to celebrate that I'm an investor in the Nairobi City Thunder!

"The Nairobi City Thunder are the first Kenyan team to qualify for the Basketball Africa League, and I'm pumped and proud to be behind them. TWENDE!

"Big weekend ahead with the start of the KNBL Finals! Wishing everyone on and off the court a great time!!"

The team was founded in 1998 - initially as NSSF Stars and later International Christian Church before switching to its current name in 2010. The 2023 acquisition of the club by Twende Sports Limited -- founded by Colin Rasmussen, Sandra Kimokoti, Kush Diriye and Stephen Domingo -- sparked a new era of success.

In 2025, Nairobi City Thunder became the first Kenyan team to play in the BAL in the fifth season of the league organized by the NBA and FIBA - a feat which they repeated in the tournament's sixth edition this year.

The BAL is transitioning to a franchise model from 2027 onwards, with permanent slots in the league on offer along with limited availability for non-franchise teams seeking to qualify.

Nairobi City Thunder will face Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) in the national finals for a third successive year, having comfortably beaten them in the previous two.

articles.headline: LaFleur at a loss for answers to Packers' offensive woes
articles.description: The Packers are off to their worst start in coach Matt LaFleur's eight seasons after they were booed off Lambeau Field on Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ラフルア監督、パッカーズのオフェンス不振に対する解決策を見出せず
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズは木曜夜にランボー・フィールドでブーイングを浴びて退場し、マット・ラフルア監督の8シーズンで最悪のスタートを切った。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The problem for the Green Bay Packers isn't just that they couldn't run the ball anywhere close to how the Atlanta Falcons did Thursday night or keep quarterback Jordan Love from getting pressured play after play. It's that through three games, they have no idea what they're good at on offense.

As a result, the Packers (1-2) are off to their worst start in coach Matt LaFleur's eight seasons after they were booed off Lambeau Field during their 35-14 loss in the home opener.

"I think we've got to continue to work with these guys and try to figure out what we do well," LaFleur said. "Because right now I don't know what we're doing well offensively."

It isn't their running game. The Packers rushed for 17 yards -- 225 yards fewer than the Falcons. They were so ineffective that they ran the ball only nine times, four each by running backs MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson and one scramble by Love. Their 17 rushing yards were tied for the third fewest by the Packers in more than 90 years.

The Packers don't have their leading rusher from the past two seasons, Josh Jacobs, who is on the commissioner exempt list, and they entered Week 3 averaging a league-worst 64.5 rushing yards per game. That number now stands at 48.7. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson had more rushing yards (194) on Thursday than the Packers have had all season (146, which is the fewest by any team through three games since the 2019 season).

"I do believe we can run the ball well," Lloyd said. "But I can't say that because we're not doing it."

The offensive line is in shambles. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele sustained a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, and when rookie Jager Burton started at left guard, it was the Packers' third different starter at that position in as many games.

While this wasn't the 15-hit battering that Love took in the Week 1 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, it was close. The Falcons were credited with 12 quarterback hits even though they sacked Love only once.

Love has completed just 52% of his passes this season, the second-lowest percentage through his team's first three games in the past 20 seasons and the lowest in the NFL since Sam Bradford in 2011 among quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts, according to ESPN Research.

The epitome of the offensive struggles came on the opening drive of the second half. Trailing 17-7, the Packers got to the Falcons' 7-yard line, where they had fourth-and-1. LaFleur went for it, but the play was doomed from the start. Love had no time and nowhere to go with the ball. His throw to the end zone was not close to Christian Watson.

"We're very frustrated tonight with the performance," said Love, who was 28-for-53 passing for 312 yards with two touchdowns and one interception. articles.headline: Penix's return revives Falcons' attack in rout of Packers
articles.description: In his first game since tearing his ACL last November, Michael Penix Jr. sparked the Falcons by passing for 256 yards with a touchdown in a 35-14 rout of the Packers at Lambeau Field.
articles.headlineJa: ペニックスの復帰でファルコンズの攻撃が復活、パッカーズに圧勝
articles.descriptionJa: 昨年11月に膝の前十字靭帯（ACL）を断裂して以来初の試合で、マイケル・ペニックス・ジュニアは256ヤードのパスと1タッチダウンを記録し、ランボー・フィールドでのパッカーズに対する35-14の圧勝劇でファルコンズを活性化させた。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Michael Penix Jr. cried in the locker room before the Atlanta Falcons' last preseason game in August, according to Falcons safety Jessie Bates III. Penix was emotional because he knew he was not ready to return from left ACL surgery last November.

On Thursday, Penix finally came back and helped lead the Falcons to a stunning 35-14 rout of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. In his first game since tearing his ACL in Week 11 last November, Penix was 18-of-25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

Bates said Penix was "dying to get back."

"I know how much it means to him," Bates said. "I know how much he means to the locker room."

Penix threw an interception on the first series but then settled down. By the second quarter, he was cruising. During the second and third quarters, Penix was 13-of-15 passing with a touchdown and 5-of-5 on third downs. The score came on a 5-yard pass to tight end Austin Hooper with 59 seconds left in the first half.

"Definitely after that interception, I started getting a rhythm, and everything started clicking," Penix said.

As it has been in his first two seasons, Penix's favorite target was wide receiver Drake London, who had nine catches for a career-high 194 yards.

"He's the definition of resiliency," London said of Penix.

The Falcons (1-2) struggled during the first two weeks of the season. With Penix not yet ready, Tua Tagovailoa was tabbed as the Week 1 starter. But Tagovailoa injured his oblique three days before the first game of the season and had to be spelled by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush.

Rush was also dealing with back spasms, and the Falcons' offense was nonexistent. They scored a combined 16 points over two games, the lowest mark in the league. Atlanta did not take a red zone snap, a skid that was finally broken after 27 straight series to begin the season, tied for the second-longest such streak in the past 45 seasons.

With Penix back under center, the Falcons' hope -- and firepower -- seemed restored. Running back Bijan Robinson had 194 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said he felt great for Penix and lauded the hard work he put in to return to the field.

"It's not easy to rehab from injuries," Stefanski said. "That's a tough thing to do when he's putting himself through the extra workouts in the weight room, the extra treatments in the training room. All those times that he's out on the field running and no one was watching. It's just him and the trainers and the medical staff. So proud of all of that. I got to witness it, and this, tonight, is something you can build on."

But the Falcons won't rest on their laurels, either.

"We got a long season to go," Penix said. "That game was far from perfect, and that's what we're striving for each and every day. So, obviously we're going to go back and look at the film, find things that we can do better."

articles.descriptionJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンとドレイク・ロンドンが猛威を振るい、アトランタはグリーンベイの本拠地開幕戦13連勝の記録を阻止した。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Have the real Atlanta Falcons stood up?

After one of the most futile offensive stretches in NFL history over the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons looked reborn in a 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night at Lambeau Field. Michael Penix Jr.'s return from a torn ACL reignited the team's offense in an impressive performance on the road in primetime against a depleted Packers team playing without edge rusher Micah Parsons (ACL) and running back Josh Jacobs (commissioner exempt list).

Penix was 18-of-25 passing for 256 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He settled down after throwing a pick on his third pass.

Penix's presence opened up the running game, which was dominant to the tune of 244 yards. Bijan Robinson had 194 of those with a touchdown and Brian Robinson Jr. added a touchdown, as well. Falcons wide receiver Drake London had nine catches for 194 yards.

The Falcons' defense stymied Packers quarterback Jordan Love all game, taking advantage of a Green Bay offensive line that was missing two starters and Jacobs.

Love was 28-of-52 for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interceptions. The Packers had only 17 rushing yards.

Over the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons, led by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, scored 16 combined points, a league low. Atlanta had 17 points by halftime Thursday night. And the Falcons were able to end a 27-drive streak without a red zone snap, which is tied for the second longest to start a season over the past 45 years.

Atlanta Falcons (1-2)

QB performance: It started off disastrously for Penix, who threw an interception on his first series of the game. But the third-year quarterback settled in nicely in his season debut once the second quarter hit. Penix was 13-of-15 passing in the second and third quarters -- with a touchdown to tight end Austin Hooper -- and a perfect 5-of-5 on third downs over that stretch.

Stat to know: In the first quarter, the Falcons ended their streak of 27 consecutive drives to start the season without taking a snap in the red zone. That is tied with the 1997 Detroit Lions for the second longest streak in the past 45 seasons, per ESPN Research. The 1992 Patriots had the longest at 34.

Trend to watch: The Falcons put star cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. (groin) on injured reserve earlier this week, but the team's secondary got a boon from the return of corner Billy Bowman Jr., who tore an Achilles last November. Bowman, C.J. Henderson and Avieon Terrell, AJ's younger brother, did a great job keeping quarterback Love in check despite the loss of Terrell, whom Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich calls one of the league's top boundary corners. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: Oct. 5 at New Orleans Saints

articles.headline: Pelinka: Lakers grateful for run with LeBron, exit 'done amicably'
articles.description: Rob Pelinka said Thursday that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with LeBron James.
articles.headlineJa: ペリンカGM：レイカーズはレブロンとの日々に感謝、退団は「円満に行われた」
articles.descriptionJa: ロブ・ペリンカGMは木曜日、レイカーズはレブロン・ジェームズと過ごした時間に今も感謝していると語った。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager Rob Pelinka said LeBron James' decision to leave the franchise this summer was "done amicably" and that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with the all-time great.

"I thought it would be appropriate at the front to express gratitude for the LeBron era here," Pelinka said Thursday before a season-opening news conference alongside Lakers coach JJ Redick.

"Clearly, new team and new players, and that's what we're going to talk about today. But we as an organization are still grateful for the run that we had with him here."

Thursday's news conference was two months to the day since James agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers and an occasion for Pelinka to share his first remarks about James' departure.

"The Lakers have become -- as they should -- a perennial playoff team," Pelinka continued, looking back at James' eight years in L.A. "Won a championship, went to the Western Conference finals. It was a great era, and we're grateful for it. I think it's important to say that at the onset as we turn into a new chapter."

James' longtime friend and agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, informed the Lakers about eight hours before the official start of free agency on June 30 that his client would be seeking a new team.

The decision was an about-face from James' previous public stance during NBA All-Star weekend in Indianapolis in February 2024.

"I am a Laker and I'm happy and been very happy being a Laker the last six years and hopefully it stays that way," James said at the time.

James' choice also came after Pelinka publicly lobbied to bring James back during an exit interview news conference with reporters in May following the Lakers' second-round exit against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

"LeBron, we probably haven't seen a player that has honored the game to the extent that he's honored the game," Pelinka said May 12. "He's given so much to his teammates, to this organization. And the thing we want to do more than anything else is honor him back. ... Any team, including ours, would love to have LeBron James on their roster."

Pelinka was asked, considering those statements from James and the Lakers in the past, why he thinks the 41-year-old star is now in Philadelphia.

"Again, we're grateful for the LeBron era," Pelinka said. "I think the communications with him this offseason were held diplomatically, professionally and honestly. I'm so thankful for the partnership that we had that continued up until this summer when a decision was made for him to play for another team. It was done amicably, professionally, gracefully. We looked at the whole thing with gratitude, because it's been an incredible era for us here."

Redick, James' former "Mind the Game" podcast co-host before stepping onto the Lakers' sidelines, did not specifically address the four-time champion's departure. Redick already showed public support for James

articles.headline: Bob Pettit, who starred at LSU and then in NBA, dies at 93
articles.description: Bob Pettit, who was named an All-Star in each of his 11 NBA seasons and was one of the greatest scorers and rebounders in league history, died, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame said Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: LSUおよびNBAのスター、ボブ・ペティット氏が93歳で死去
articles.descriptionJa: NBAの11シーズンすべてでオールスターに選出され、リーグ史上屈指のスコアラーかつリバウンダーであったボブ・ペティット氏が死去したと、ネイスミス・バスケットボール殿堂が木曜日に発表した。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Bob Pettit, an imposing scorer and rebounder for the St. Louis Hawks and winner of the NBA's first MVP award in 1956, has died. He was 93.

Pettit's alma mater, LSU, announced Thursday that he died a day earlier. The university did not provide a cause of death.

Pettit was an All-American at LSU before going on to the NBA, where he was an All-Star for each of his 11 seasons, all with the Hawks. He led them to the 1958 championship over the mighty Boston Celtics, the Hawks' lone title.

He was also the NBA MVP in 1959 and was the MVP of the All-Star Game four times, an achievement matched only by Los Angeles Lakers great Kobe Bryant.

Pettit was a force at a time when the NBA featured the likes of Wilt Chamberlain, Bill Russell, Oscar Robertson and Elgin Baylor. But it was also before the NBA was widely seen on television, and Pettit -- playing in a smaller market -- was denied a larger audience.

At 6-foot-9 and 205 pounds, Pettit was a physical presence at power forward before such a position became part of basketball's vocabulary. He rarely missed a game. He also played center and was one of the first big men who did not play solely with his back to the basket.

Pettit was the Rookie of the Year in 1954-55, the last season the Hawks played in Milwaukee before moving to St. Louis.

He captured the MVP the next season, leading the league in scoring at 25.7 points a game. He also was the NBA's scoring leader in 1959 at 29.2 points.

He retired after the 1964-65 season with career averages of 26.4 points and 16.2 rebounds. At that time, he was the NBA's career leader in points (20,880) and second in rebounds (12,849).

He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1970.

"Lean, graceful, and always well-conditioned, Bob Pettit's physical build made him one of the first big men to play facing the basket," reads Pettit's biographical profile at the Hall of Fame. "But Pettit's resolve set him apart from his peers; he simply would not be outworked."

On social media Thursday, the Hall of Fame called Pettit a "sleek, skilled big man who revolutionized the forward position," adding that he was a "true giant of the game." 

Robert Lee Pettit Jr. was born on Dec. 12, 1932, in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. His father worked in law enforcement and served as East Baton Rouge Parish sheriff. Pettit was a late bloomer in basketball, not making the Baton Rouge High School varsity until his junior season.

As a senior, he led Baton Rouge to a state championship and wound up with more than a dozen college offers. He chose to stay home and starred at LSU as a sophomore, an era when players could not join the varsity until then.

He led the SEC in scoring all three of his seasons, with averages of 25.5 points as a sophomore, 24.9 as a junior and 31.4 as a senior.
